findings.title: Possible dynamic Python evaluation
findings.root_cause: A direct eval/exec call-like pattern was observed after comment/string masking.
findings.input_to_impact: Analyst must trace input control, reachability and business impact.
findings.prerequisites: No syntax, scope, taint or reachability proof. Shadowed names or invalid code can produce false positives.
findings.mitigations: Not evaluated. Inspect validation, authorization, isolation and compensating controls.
findings.evidence: Lexical pattern matched; arguments and source text omitted.
findings.remediation: Trace input reachability and builtin shadowing; replace dynamic evaluation with explicit parsing.

missions.title: Independent application review
missions.objective: Validate source-level candidates and document remediation. Workflow: code.
steps: Review the 1 unresolved ledger candidate(s), inspect source in your controlled system and trace input reachability.
Trace inputs through authentication, authorization and trust boundaries.
Attempt to refute each candidate using validation, reachability and compensating controls.
Record a verdict with evidence and a scoped regression test before declaring a fix.
missions.deliverable: An evidence-backed review ledger and remediation checklist.
limitations: Planning guidance only; requires a qualified analyst and separate approval for live actions.
No executable agents, scanners, model inference or upstream security tools are running.

records.summary: 1 unresolved candidate(s) from limited browser-local checks. Human validation required; this is not a security certification.
coverage: Limited lexical regex/pattern nomination: quoted strings/comments masked for call detection, direct eval/exec, simple subprocess import aliases and bounded multiline literal shell=True arguments.

No Python AST or syntax parser, scope/rebinding resolution, taint/dataflow, dependency audit, execution or exploit validation. Wildcard/dynamic imports, f-string expressions, complex assignments and computed shell flags may be missed.
Maximum 500 call-like constructs, 8192 characters per subprocess call and 100 candidates. No matches do not establish security; manual review is required.
